findings.title: wasm32-unknown-unknown build regression — getrandom requires "js" feature; 4 CI checks newly FAILING vs base 340391ab
findings.location: crates/benten-graph/Cargo.toml dependency chain (new benten-crypto-suite dep → ml-dsa + chacha20poly1305 + ed25519-dalek + x25519-dalek → getrandom 0.2.17 without js feature gate)
evidence: PR #1323 4 wasm32 failures: (a) `T8 benten-napi wasm32-unknown-unknown` (WASM Checks) — FAILURE; (b) `bundle + size cap + headless smoke` (WASM Browser) — FAILURE; (c) `build wasm32-unknown-unknown bundle` (Cross-Browser Determinism) — FAILURE; (d) `wasm32 (wasip1 runtime + unknown-unknown compile)` (CI) — FAILURE.
Base SHA 340391ab on main: ALL FOUR workflows GREEN (verified via `gh run list --workflow=... --branch main`); `WASM Checks` SUCCESS at 340391ab, 8883f789, 8fec3cbc, 1d087433, c9c11c56.

Reproduced LOCALLY: `cargo check -p benten-napi --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features benten-engine/browser-backend --no-default-features` → identical `error: the wasm*-unknown-unknown targets are not supported by default, you may need to enable the "js" feature` from getrandom v0.2.17.

Root cause: PR #1323 adds `benten-crypto-suite = { path = ... }` as an UN-CONDITIONAL dependency of `benten-graph` (line 102 of crates/benten-graph/Cargo.toml). benten-graph is on the benten-napi → benten-engine → benten-graph wasm32-unknown-unknown build chain (per CLAUDE.md baked-in #17 thin-client commitment). benten-crypto-suite hard-depends on ml-dsa/chacha20poly1305/ed25519-dalek/x25519-dalek, which transitively pull `getrandom` without the `js` feature.
G-CORE-3a CANARY (PR #1319) introduced `benten-crypto-suite` itself but the wasm CI stayed green because no wasm-target-reachable crate depended on it; this PR is the first wasm-reachable consumer.
findings.production_impact: Browser-target builds (CLAUDE.md baked-in #17 shape b — thin compute surface) DO NOT COMPILE post-merge. This is a direct violation of the thin-client commitment + breaks the embedded-webview / browser-tab deployment shapes.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW per HARD RULE 12. Two valid resolutions: (a) make the `benten-crypto-suite` dep target-conditional on `benten-graph` — `[target.'cfg(not(all(target_arch = "wasm32", target_os = "unknown")))'.dependencies] benten-crypto-suite = { path = ... }` — and `#[cfg_attr(target_arch="wasm32"+target_os="unknown", allow(...))]`-gate the `aead_wrap` + AEAD-wrap branch of `put_node_with_context`; OR (b) propagate `getrandom = { version = "0.2", features = ["js"] }` (and 0.3 equivalent) as an explicit dep in `benten-crypto-suite` under `cfg(all(target_arch="wasm32", target_os="unknown"))`. (a) is the lower-risk path — wasm32-unknown-unknown is the thin-client target that fundamentally has no per-DID-AEAD wrap path (BrowserBackend rejects namespaced writes at GraphError::NamespacedWriteUnsupported anyway); (b) is the broader fix that lets the integration crate compile on browser. Recommend (a) as a quick-fix, with (b) named-now into `docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md §3.10 G-CORE-3e` (where the K_principal-per-DID seam will need browser consideration anyway).
findings.named_destination_if_b_chosen: docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md §3.10 (G-CORE-3e entry already exists; add a sub-bullet 'browser-target getrandom feature gating').

Per-finding closure pins (dim 2 / pim-2 §3.6b sub-rule 4): pins are surgical — separate pin for AAD-binds-plaintext-CID (tf3d_aad_binds_plaintext_cid_rebinding_attack_defeated), separate pin for chunk-index AAD (tf3d_cross_chunk_rebinding_fails_aad_binds_chunk_index), separate pin for chunk-size = IROH_BLOCK_SIZE constant (tf3d_iroh_block_size_is_16_kib_exactly), separate pin for the two-CID-mapping durability across redb-reopen (tf3d_two_cid_mapping_durable_across_reopen). The G-CORE-3e named destination at docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md §3.10 (line 166) is well-formed: 'Includes the K(N) production-source swap-in (per HARD RULE 12 clause-(b) BELONGS-NAMED-NOW)' with explicit identification of the 1-call-site replacement at the put-path + the read-path read_decrypt_inner; both already point at the same `derive_test_seam_key_from_cid` helper so the swap-in IS a clean 1-line change. CLAUDE.md baked-in #5 crypto-agility preserved (dim 9): aead_wrap.rs module head doc comment explicitly states 'Every AEAD operation routes through `benten_crypto_suite::aead::wrap` / `::unwrap` / `::aad_whole_content` / `::aad_per_chunk`. This module is glue: threshold dispatch + chunk slicing + envelope packaging.' Verified: no direct `use chacha20poly1305::*` / `use blake3` / etc. in aead_wrap.rs body; the only crypto-primitive routing is via `suite_wrap` / `suite_unwrap` / `suite_aad_whole_content` / `suite_aad_per_chunk` aliases. Codepoint dispatch via `KeyMaterial::from_bytes_for_test(envelope.cipher_codepoint, key)` in `make_key_material_matching` preserves the codepoint-dispatch arm (codepoint mismatch surfaces typed `AeadError::Unsupported`, never silent fallback).

Inv-11 strengthening structural (dim 10): partition-before-crypto order is STRUCTURAL — the namespaced AEAD-wrap path in `put_node_with_context` happens INSIDE the `if let Some(did) = ctx.namespace_did.as_ref()` arm (the partition decision is made first via the WriteContext shape, then the AEAD-wrap fires within that arm); the read path `read_via_two_cid_scoped` consults `two_cid_lookup_scoped` whose key is `d:<did>:m:<plaintext_cid>` — a cross-DID caller misses at the partition-prefix layer with `Ok(None)` BEFORE any AEAD work. Verified by the tf3d_cross_did_returns_notfound_not_aead_error pin which explicitly asserts the error variant is `NotFound` and EXPLICITLY rejects `AeadAuthenticationFailed`. No encryption-before-partition inversion observed.

8-site TF-1 test updates (dim 11): preserves G-CORE-1's contracts. The change is `let cid = backend.put_node_with_context(&node, &ctx).expect(...)` → `backend.put_node_with_context(&node, &ctx).expect(...); let cid = node.cid().unwrap()`. G-CORE-1's contracts (label_index keyed on plaintext_cid, ChangeEvent.cid = plaintext_cid, scoped().get_node(plaintext) returns Node) ALL key on plaintext_cid which IS what `node.cid()` returns. Verified: the put-return value-change from plaintext_cid → ciphertext_cid for namespaced writes does NOT propagate to any non-test production caller. The only PRODUCTION namespaced `with_namespace_did(Some(...))` call site in workspace is `crates/benten-graph/src/browser_backend.rs:736` which is itself inside `#[cfg(test)]` — i.e. NO production caller currently exercises the namespaced-write return value, so the surface-change has zero production blast radius. All 9 production engine callers of `put_node_with_context` use `WriteContext::privileged_for_engine_api()` (verified) which has `namespace_did: None`, hitting the legacy un-namespaced path (return = plaintext_cid unchanged). The TF-1 updates are minimal + correct.
